result.title: Learning the Missing Derivative: Neural Multiple-Scattering Operators for Inverse Volume Rendering
result.summary: Reconstructing optically thick media from photographs requires modeling multiple scattering and its response to changes in extinction. Frozen-source tomography discards this derivative; differentiable path tracing estimates it through expensive, noisy sampling. We instead predict the multiple-scattering field with a neural operator and differentiate through it during inverse rendering, while computing transmittance and single scattering directly. A further challenge arises during optimization: an operator that predicts the field accurately on held-out media can still produce poor derivatives at the density states visited by the optimizer. We address this by fine-tuning on states generated during inversions driven by the operator, using Monte Carlo scattering-field supervision. On held-out optically thick clouds, our method improves relighting over frozen-source tomography at equal time and outperforms differentiable path tracing given substantially more time. Training on inversion trajectories also improves derivative alignment at visited states and reduces optimization drift.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用神经算子预测光学厚介质中的多重散射场，并在逆渲染中直接对其求导；针对「留出数据上预测准确、但在优化器实际访问的密度状态上导数失配」的问题，用逆渲染轨迹生成的状态配合蒙特卡洛散射场监督做微调。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「前向预测准确不等于导数可用、需在实际访问状态上校正」与 latent 推理中状态表征看似合理但梯度或贡献分配错位的失败模式可能同构，按自生成轨迹状态再训练的监督思路也可供核查。
